entries.name: Before the heavy rains
entries.when: While the ground is dry and workable, before the first heavy rain.
do_this: Walk the plot and look for white crust, hard packed patches and wide cracks.
Break the hard top to about a hand's depth with a spade or a pick.
Open shallow drains running downhill so rain can leave instead of pooling.
Mix in dung, ash and chopped straw. Use gypsum only if a local farmer says it suits your ground.
watch_for: Hard ground a stick will not enter.
White powder drying on the surface.
Low spots where water always stands.

entries.name: The first heavy rains
entries.when: After the first heavy rain, and again after each heavy rain.
do_this: Let the rain soak the ground and run out through the drains, carrying salt with it.
Keep the low spots from pooling by leading the water away.
Check the surface once it dries. If the white crust returns, flush again.
watch_for: Water standing in the dips.
The white crust returning as the ground dries.
Cloudy water leaving the low end.

entries.name: The warm wet season
entries.when: Through the warm wet season, once the soil crumbles and the salt has eased.
do_this: Sow the grasses when the soil crumbles in your hand.
Sow the rice where a shallow layer of water can be held.
Sow pearl millet and sorghum on the warmer, drier patches.
Sow sesbania and dig it back into the soil before it seeds.
watch_for: Leaves yellowing in ground that stays wet.
Seedlings toppling over at the base.
Small insects gathering under the leaves.

entries.name: As the rains ease
entries.when: As the heavy rains ease and the ground starts to dry and crumble.
do_this: Sow barley, mustard, sugarbeet and oats once the puddles have gone.
Keep the drains open so no water stands around the roots.
Keep the seedbed loose so the young shoots come up through soft ground.
watch_for: Ground that sticks to the spade instead of crumbling.
White powder spreading over the leaves.

entries.name: The hot dry spell
entries.when: Through the hot dry spell, when the ground dries and hardens.
do_this: Harvest the grain when the heads droop, turn brown and rattle.
Keep the young trees watered and shade their base with straw.
Mulch bare ground with straw and ash to hold moisture.
Watch for the white crust returning and flush it after any rain.
watch_for: Plants wilting with hard dry ground below the surface.
Brown and orange spots spreading on the leaves.

entries.name: The cool dry spell
entries.when: Through the cool dry months, when the nights turn cold and the days mild.
do_this: Cut the fodder when the grass reaches your knee, and again as it recovers.
Lift sugarbeet and gather mustard seed when the leaves yellow or the pods rattle.
Store roots in a pit covered with straw and soil.
watch_for: Moss and sorrel spreading in damp corners.
A sour smell in the soil.

entries.name: Planting the slow trees
entries.when: At the start of the rains, or the start of the warm season for the palm.
do_this: Dig a deep pit and mix good soil, dung, ash and straw into it.
Set the young tree into soaked ground and water it well.
Cover the base with straw and ash and keep animals off with a ring of thorn.
watch_for: Dry ground below a wet top, which stops roots going down.
Animals rubbing against or grazing the young trees.

entries.name: Every season, whatever the weather
entries.when: All through the year, in every season.
do_this: Pull weeds while they are small and before they seed, then let them dry as mulch.
Keep the ground covered so it does not crust, blow or wash away.
Check a pinch of soil in vinegar and in baking soda now and then to see which one fizzes.
When anything looks new or strange, ask a local elder or farmer.
watch_for: Weeds setting seed.
Bare ground left after harvest.
Any change in the smell, colour or feel of the soil.
